description: Working from a written specification that humans review and agents plan, break into tasks and implement from.
The common SDD pipeline: requirements first, then the technical design, then small tasks that reference requirements, then implementation proven by tests.
One row per requirement with the tasks that implement it and the tests that verify it. It shows what is unplanned, untested or orphaned.
Levels of commitment: a spec that guides one change, a spec maintained with the feature, or a spec that is the only artifact humans edit.
Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax: templates such as "When <trigger>, the system shall <response>" that make each requirement testable.
The spec, the tasks and the tests no longer describe the same system: references to removed ids, behavior nobody specified.
